A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-based temporal video grounding work, renamed from TimeZero to Time-R1. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A-E.

before.justification: v1 reports original Charades-STA and ActivityNet evaluations, training/test-time reasoning ablations, and cross-dataset generalization results in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: v2 reports original grounding and video-QA evaluations, TVGBench results, component ablations, model-size comparisons, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v1 uses GRPO with raw IoU and format rewards. v2 introduces timestamp-aware tIoU, Gaussian difficulty-based data selection, dynamic removal of easy samples during multi-epoch training, and supervised CoT cold-start training. Appendix B also explicitly adopts DAPO's token-level loss instead of GRPO's sample-level loss. These substantially revise the training procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond Charades-STA and ActivityNet, v2 introduces training on a curated multi-source Internet-video corpus and evaluates TVGBench, incorporating HiREST, EgoNLQ, and TaCoS coverage. It also evaluates multiple-choice video QA on MVBench, TempCompass, EgoSchema, and VideoMME, substantially expanding domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated comparators including UniVTG and VTimeLLM, adds 2D-TAN to the Charades comparison and ChatVTG to ActivityNet, and removes DRN from ActivityNet. TVGBench comparisons introduce Gemini-2.5-Pro, while Figure 4 adds SFT-LoRA. v1's VideoChat-T matches v2's TimeSuite through the reference and retained fine-tuned scores.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from one epoch with batch size 1 to five reinforcement fine-tuning epochs with batch size 8 and two epochs for downstream fine-tuning. v2 introduces curated-data zero-shot evaluations, a 3B model configuration, mIoU reporting, and video-QA accuracy protocols. The stated Charades/ActivityNet splits and 2-FPS input sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds ablations of tIoU, Gaussian filtering, multi-epoch training, sample filtering, cold start, KL/CoT, and DAPO versus GRPO, alongside model scaling, semantic-category diagnostics, inference timing, and extensive case studies. v1's explicit training/test-time CoT matrix and Charades-trained ActivityNet generalization table are not retained; related questions are examined through different experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's dataset-distribution plots and training curves do not introduce experimental uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Under revised training, v2 replaces the fine-tuned Charades R1@0.3/0.5/0.7 results of 83.3/72.5/47.9 with 82.8/72.2/50.1, and ActivityNet's 68.6/47.3/26.9 with 73.3/55.6/34.0 (v1 Tables 1-2; v2 Table 1). These are replacement results, not controlled same-setting gains. Numerous zero-shot, TVGBench, QA, ablation, category-level, and timing results are newly reported.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 4 introduces a mathematical definition of tIoU: ordinary IoU multiplied by two timestamp-error penalties normalized by video duration. This is a limited formal extension of the reward definition. The background GRPO equations are substantially retained, and neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers on pure-RL reasoning and state-of-the-art Charades grounding. v2 defines three contributions—Time-R1, TimeRFT, and TVGBench—and adds claims about data efficiency using 2.5K training examples, broader zero-shot and fine-tuned performance, and transfer to general video QA. Its framework also accommodates supervised cold-start training, revising the pure-RL framing.

C2.justification: The main explanation shifts toward SFT's excessive penalties for approximately correct timestamps and resulting overfitting. v2 adds interpretations concerning curriculum learning, cold-start hallucination suppression, and the KL/interpretability tradeoff. Appendices A and C newly discuss speed, missed motion, ultra-long-video limitations, and weaknesses on complex instructions and object-related grounding.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly supplies response-group size, KL coefficient, optimizer and learning-rate schedules, gradient accumulation, cold-start sample count, LoRA parameters, and baseline preprocessing. Figures 11 and 15 disclose prompts. Hardware changes from four A800 GPUs to eight A100 GPUs; training time and a vLLM implementation are documented. The repository pointer is replaced by a project-page pointer.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the research context, replacing much of the general CoT discussion with an RLHF/RLVR distinction and positioning against MM-Eureka, Visual-RFT, Reason-RFT, and short-video RL approaches. DAPO and numerous training-data and benchmark references are added, while several earlier grounding and CoT works disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around the expanded contributions. Dedicated TimeRFT and TVGBench subsections and Appendices A-E reorganize the narrative. The title, model terminology, author list, and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column template, replaces the opening illustration, and redraws the method comparison. Separate benchmark tables become a combined table distinguishing zero-shot and fine-tuned results. New distribution charts, training plots, diagnostic tables, prompt panels, and qualitative figures substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Appendix B substantially remedies v1's sparse reproducibility information, while component ablations and semantic-category analyses make the expanded method more testable and expose specific weaknesses. The broader generalization evaluations and explicit limitations also improve the evidence supporting the paper. Reporting problems remain: Section 4.3 misattributes TVGBench values from Figure 4 to ActivityNet, and Appendices B and D inconsistently describe the Gaussian filtering parameter. These defects qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in documentation and empirical scrutiny.
